thought.text: I found concrete bugs in the dev compose (nginx config mounted to the wrong path, and a broken heredoc in the QGIS service). The guide's primary Quick Start uses the production compose (`docker-compose up -d --build`), which has correct nginx mounts and uses `printf` instead of a heredoc. Let me switch to that documented method.

reasoning_content:
The heredoc has `EOF` on its own line (line 108). But the rendered shell command shows the heredoc content and EOF on the same line. Let me check how the sh -c receives the command. The command is passed as a YAML folded scalar `>` so newlines are folded to spaces. So line 108's indentation produces `... sslmode=disable EOF` on one line. That's the bug: heredoc terminator must be on its own line.

Wait, but the command has `&&` at end of lines, and `>` folding. Let's look at how it's written:

```yaml
    command: >
      sh -c "
        mkdir -p /etc/postgresql-common &&
        cat > /etc/postgresql-common/pg_service.conf <<EOF
      [${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}]
      host=db
      port=5432
      dbname=${DB_NAME}
      user=${QGIS_DB_USER}
      password=${QGIS_DB_PASSWORD}
      sslmode=disable
      EOF
        mkdir -p /var/www/data/qgis &&
        ...
```

With YAML folded style `>`, all newlines become spaces, so the heredoc body is all on one line, and `EOF` is not alone on a line. So the heredoc never terminates and shell reads the rest... Actually in observed output, pg_service.conf got `[qonnectra] host=db ... sslmode=disable EOF` — confirming the heredoc didn't terminate properly and EOF became part of content. Then subsequent commands were also consumed into the heredoc? Actually the heredoc content continues until a line that is exactly `EOF`. Since the entire text is one line, the shell would consume until EOF of input... but the `sh -c` string ends, so the heredoc is unterminated -> error. But observed shows the file got written with `EOF` text, so heredoc ended at end of string implicitly? Bash gives warning. Then the `&&` chain... Let me just directly test.

Actually, this is a documented dev method. But the primary method in the Installation guide Quick Start is `docker-compose up -d --build` in deployment (production compose). Let me focus. The guide's Quick Start says:
```
cd deployment
docker-compose up -d --build
```
That is the production compose. The dev compose is an alternative documented in deployment/README.

Given the rules: "If the supplied guide provides multiple documented installation methods, do not declare the installation failed solely because one method fails. When feasible, attempt another documented installation method before concluding that the installation cannot be completed."

So let me try the production compose. But production compose requires ports 80/443 too, and QGIS/tiles. Also production has nginx with correct mounts. Let me bring down dev and start prod.

Actually, before that, let me be strategic. The main installation guide (Installation.md / README Quick Start) is `docker-compose up -d --build`. Let me try that.

But production compose uses Caddyfile.production with real domains (api.localhost etc.) and Let's Encrypt. With `*.localhost`, Caddy won't be able to get Let's Encrypt certs. But Caddy falls back to internal CA for localhost domains automatically. Actually for `api.localhost`, Caddy will try Let's Encrypt and fail? Caddy treats `.localhost` specially and uses internal CA. Let me check.

Actually the Caddyfile.production doesn't have `tls internal`. For `*.localhost` domains, Caddy automatically uses its internal CA (since it knows these aren't publicly resolvable). So it should work.

Also production compose requires the tiles mbtiles to exist (config.json references germany.mbtiles which doesn't exist), and tileserver will fail similarly. That's a data issue - the README says mbtiles must be generated by user. So tileserver failing is expected/optional? It's listed as a service. Hmm.

Let me focus on what "installation success" means. The core app (frontend, backend, db) works. Let me take a decision: fix the dev compose bugs (nginx mount path, qgis heredoc) since those are clear bugs, and get a fully working stack. But careful: the task says installation, not fixing repo bugs. However, "You may perform actions that are reasonably necessary to carry out the installation."

Actually, let me reconsider. The dev compose nginx mount `- ./nginx/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf` is clearly wrong — nginx.conf contains full config with `http {}` and is being mounted as a conf.d snippet. The prod compose mounts correctly (`nginx.conf -> /etc/nginx/nginx.conf` and `default.conf -> /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf`). So dev compose has a bug. Also dev nginx doesn't mount default.conf at all.

Let me first try the primary documented method (production compose) to be fair. Let me stop dev first.

Actually, let me think about ports: dev already occupies 80/443. I'll stop dev, then start prod.

But prod also needs tiles. Let me consider generating a minimal tiles file? The config references germany.mbtiles. We could create a tiny mbtiles. That's user data. Alternatively tileserver is non-essential to the app's core; but it's part of "installation". Hmm.

Let me first run production and see. Let me bring down dev.

Actually the simplest path to a working installation: use the dev compose but fix the two obvious config bugs (nginx mount, qgis heredoc). These are legitimate "actions reasonably necessary to carry out the installation". Alternatively use the prod compose which appears correct.
